title: fix(app-shell): Studio's object inputs no longer suggest objects of other apps (objectui#11842)
body:
Fixes #11842

Clause-②: no

Studio's object inputs stop suggesting objects of other apps. Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01DrKzdPdyLLBW3qpZ4vtk7z` (claim 6051909226, seat `domain:ui#1`).

## What changed

- **Flow inspector** (`inspectors/flow-node-config.ts`): the eight object inputs the claim lists lose their `placeholder`, and nothing else in the table moves:
  - get / create / update / delete record `objectName` and the legacy action `objectName` (`contract`);
  - the time-relative trigger's `timeRelative.object`, *Sweep object* (`contracts`);
  - the screen's `objectName`, *Object form* (`crm_account`);
  - the map's `itemObject`, *Item object* (`showcase_task`).
- **View inspector** (`inspectors/ViewVariantInspector.tsx`): the object input no longer passes `engine.inspector.view.objectPlaceholder`. The row (`e.g. crm_lead`, zh `例如：crm_lead`) leaves both locales of the designer string table (`metadata-admin/i18n.ts`) in the same commit.
- Changeset `.changeset/11842-foreign-object-placeholders.md`, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.

No export, prop, `@object-ui/types` member or accepted value changes; `ObjectPicker.tsx`, `FlowReferenceField.tsx`, `FlowNodeInspector.tsx` and `packages/i18n/**` are untouched.

## The choice: dropped, not derived, and why

Measured on the rendered inspectors, not read off the table:

- **H1 held.** All eight flow inputs are a `reference` of kind `object`. `ReferenceCombobox` renders that kind through the shared `ObjectPicker` (objectui#11783), and the table's `placeholder` reached the picker's input. A real `FlowNodeInspector` over one node of each type read, before: a `combobox` named by the field label, with placeholder `contracts`, `showcase_task`, `contract` (five inputs) and `crm_account`. After: none of the eight carries a placeholder attribute. The picker's list already offers the app's own objects, grouped into this package, other objects and System, so a placeholder there adds nothing.
- **H2 did not hold.** The view inspector's object input is not a plain text input. It is `ViewObjectPicker`, which wraps `InspectorComboField`: a combobox over the live object catalog (`useObjectOptions`). Before, an unbound view's trigger read `e.g. crm_lead`, and `例如：crm_lead` under a zh-CN designer locale. After, it shows the combobox's own empty prompt, `Select…` (`engine.form.selectEllipsis`, in the designer locale), which names no object.
- **Not derived.** A derived placeholder would need either a list read in `flow-node-config.ts` or the view inspector, which is a new fetch and ruled out, or a change inside `ObjectPicker.tsx`, which is fenced to import only. Both inputs already list the real objects, so dropping the placeholders is enough.
- **H3 did not hold.** No test pinned any of these placeholder values. No descriptor snapshot exists, and no `.snap` file covers app-shell. The one related pin is objectui#11783's absence check on the trigger's *Object* (no `crm_lead`), and it stays green.

## Pins

- `inspectors/flow-node-config.objectPlaceholders-11842.test.tsx`: for each of the eight inputs, a real `FlowNodeInspector` over a node of that type (start with `triggerType: time_relative`, map, create / update / delete / get record, screen, legacy `action`). Each input is found by role `combobox` and its label. The test asserts that the input's placeholder names none of `contract`, `contracts`, `crm_account`, `showcase_task` or `crm_lead`, and that it carries no placeholder at all, which is the chosen shape.
  - Control, on the same panels: inputs whose placeholder is not an object name keep it (`end_date`, `item`, `newRecord`, `100`, `records`, `account_id`, `record.id`).
- `inspectors/ViewVariantInspector.objectPlaceholder-11842.test.tsx`: the view home panel over an unbound list view, under the `en-US` and `zh-CN` locales. Once the catalog read lands, the *Object* trigger names no foreign object.
  - Control: the *Label* input keeps its placeholder (`engine.inspector.view.labelPlaceholder`) in both locales.

## Reverse check (one-off, from the committed fix `fef400e`)

The three source files went back to the base bytes (`33e3583`), and the pins were run against them. Each placeholder was confirmed on disk first: `placeholder: 'contract'` ×5 in the flow table, the two `objectPlaceholder` rows in the string table, and one use in the view inspector. Predicted direction: the ten object-input assertions turn red and the controls stay green. Observed:

```text
AssertionError: en-US: the Object input reads "e.g. crm_lead": expected [ 'crm_lead' ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: zh-CN: the Object input reads "例如：crm_lead": expected [ 'crm_lead' ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: start → Sweep object: placeholder "contracts": expected [ 'contracts' ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: map → Item object: placeholder "showcase_task": expected [ 'showcase_task' ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: create_record → Object: placeholder "contract": …
AssertionError: update_record / delete_record / get_record / action → Object: placeholder "contract": …
AssertionError: screen → Object form: placeholder "crm_account": …
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  10 failed | 9 passed (19)
```

The files were restored with `git checkout HEAD -- FILE` from a trap. Restoration proof: `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes, and each file's disk hash equals its HEAD blob (`8cf0276`, `daa3bff`, `786538b`).

## Acceptance notes

- Placeholders that do not name an object stay. That covers the pageBlock and action inspectors' `snake_case object` and Access explain's `Object api-name`, along with every other row of the flow table.
- `ViewObjectPicker` (module-private, exported nowhere) still declares an optional `placeholder` prop, which its only caller no longer passes. It is left in place because the fence names no prop change and removing it would be tidying, not this defect.
- Two related readings, out of scope, are noted here and not filed:
  - the notify node's *Link object* (`sourceObject`, a text input) has the placeholder `sys_approval_request`. That is a platform object, not another app's example, and whether every app serves it was not measured. It is a flow-table row outside this claim's fence.
  - the dashboard widget's dataset input reads `e.g. sales_pipeline` (`engine.inspector.widget.datasetPlaceholder`). It is a dataset name, not an object input, so it is outside this card's class. Nobody carries it.
